subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: finance options and GPU cost scenarios
messages:
From: Ava Cole <ava@omnihealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@omnihealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing and potential commit

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We are moving toward a proof-of-concept where we expect ~120 qps at 8k average prompt length for our clinical summarization pipeline, but the workload is bursty (spikes to ~400 qps for short windows).

We need a sense of committed capacity options (monthly reserved GPU hours / fleet sizing) and how sensitive pricing would be if GPU spot/market costs move. Our procurement lead Danielle is copied. High-level asks:
- Recommended reserved capacity tiers for the described profile
- Pricing bands and discount thresholds for 6/12/24-month commitments
- How Redwood manages capacity overflow (bursting to on-demand/dedicated) and what incremental costs look like

Can you send an initial options memo and an example cost-sensitivity model? We have a budget cadence late-Nov and would like to land an approach before the end of the month.

Best,
Ava
Ava Cole
Head of ML Engineering, OmniHealth Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ava Cole <ava@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Danielle Park <dpark@omnihealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and potential commit

Ava — thanks for the clear note and timeline. Putting a short options memo together (attached) and a sensitivity workbook that models per-token cost across different GPU spot-price scenarios. High-level summary here first:

1) Sizing recommendations
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 x A100-80GB equiv nodes for steady-state ~120 qps at 8k avg.
- Burst buffer: allow autoscale to add up to +20 nodes for short spikes; we can keep burst capacity as on-demand with pre-warmed containers to reduce cold-starts.

2) Commit term and pricing bands (illustrative)
- 6 month: ~8% discount off list per-token rate for reserve of baseline pool
- 12 month: ~14% discount
- 24 month: ~20% discount with lower unit pricing if committed GPU-hours exceed threshold X

3) GPU cost sensitivity
- If underlying GPU spot market moves +25%, unit economics worsen by ~10-12% unless customer accepts larger committed hours or we apply deeper commit discounts.
- We can offer a cap/floor addendum for 12+ month deals where Redwood absorbs up to a 10% delta; above that we revisit pricing (requires leadership approval).

I attached the memo (OmniHealth_reserved_options_v1.pdf) and the sensitivity model (gpu_pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx). I've also sketched a draft SOW for dedicated deployment so your procurement team can start internal review.

Next step: if the 12mo+ cap proposal is interesting, I should loop in Jordan for approval on the cap/floor and any deeper discounts — need fast-track finance sign-off for the absorption clause.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: OmniHealth_reserved_options_v1.pdf (summary of tiers, assumptions)
Attachment: gpu_pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx (Excel model: scenarios tab, assumptions tab)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing and potential commit — discount/cap guidance

Looping in finance ops and Laura for quick guidance. Saw Marcus' memo. Quick thoughts:

- 6/12/24 bands look directionally fine.
- For any cap/floor where Redwood absorbs variance, we should limit exposure: suggest cap absorption up to 8% for 12mo and 5% for 6mo. 24mo could go to 12% but only with an anchor commitment (e.g., 1.5x baseline GPU-hours minimum).
- Any absorption clause >10% requires VP sales approval.
- Approvals needed: Discount levels beyond 18% list must be signed off by finance; anything >22% needs CRO/Jordan sign-off.

Marcus — can you quantify exposure at the 8/12% absorption levels in the existing sensitivity workbook? Laura, can you do a quick sanity check on the SOW pricing assumptions?

-JB

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ava Cole <ava@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Danielle Park <dpark@omnihealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and potential commit — updated scenarios attached

Thanks Jordan — I updated the sensitivity model with the 5/8/12% absorption bands as requested and added a dashboard tab that shows monthly expected variance to Redwood under each band. Key callouts:

- Under a 12mo, 14% list discount commit, absorbing up to 8% of spot increase results in estimated Redwood exposure of ~$46k/month in worst-case scenario modeled (peak-market stress, see scenarios tab).
- We can mitigate by making burst nodes billed as usage (pass-through) above baseline; that reduces Redwood exposure by ~60% but pushes variability to the customer.
- If OmniHealth wants firm load protection, the commercial asks for a 24mo term with a 1.2x committed-hours growth collar — that gets us to a stable unit price and allows deeper discounting.

Attachments: gpu_pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx (updated), SOW_dedicated-deployment_draft.docx

Ava — let me know if you want a short call this week to walk the model with Danielle. Happy to run through assumptions live.

Best,
Marcus

From: Danielle Park <dpark@omnihealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ava Cole <ava@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and potential commit — next steps

Thanks Marcus — the model helps. Procurement prefers a mix: baseline reserved for predictability (12mo) + on-demand burst passthrough. We will review the SOW and share internal pricing guidance next week.

One quick ask: can Redwood provide a short clause in the SOW that clarifies how surge billing is calculated and provides a monthly cap on pass-through for initial quarter? That will help our CFO sign-off.

We'll target an internal decision by Nov 30.

Regards,
Danielle Park
Senior Procurement Manager, OmniHealth Analytics
